clue.text: Generously rewarded for doing a top job?

definitions.text: Generously rewarded for doing a top job?

parts.words: Generously rewarded for doing a top job?
parts.note: a top job is one done high up, like a steeplejack's, so the pay is literally for working up high as well as being lavish

explanation.walkthrough: Read 'a top job' as work at a great height and the phrase describes pay for being up there; read it as an executive post and it is plain generous pay.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone lavishly remunerated for a senior post earns a large salary.

clue.text: Event that gives runners a chance to warm up

definitions.text: Event that gives runners a chance to warm up

parts.words: Event that gives runners a chance to warm up
parts.note: a qualifying round in athletics, where 'warm up' is read literally as getting hot

explanation.walkthrough: 'Warm up' suggests limbering exercises before a race, but the word for a preliminary race also means warmth.
explanation.definitionFit: A preliminary qualifying race in athletics shares its name with warmth.

clue.text: It comes as a sudden blow

definitions.text: It comes as a sudden blow

parts.words: It comes as a sudden blow
parts.note: a sudden blow sounds like a shock or a punch, but here it is the wind blowing briefly and strongly

explanation.walkthrough: 'Blow' looks like a setback or punch; it is the wind blowing.
explanation.definitionFit: A brief rush of wind is exactly a sudden blowing.

clue.text: Wild revels for prize bars, we hear

definitions.note: 'prize' sounds like 'prise', to force open, so these are bars for prising

indicators.note: wild revels are disorderly, so the letters of the word are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: Unruly partying earns someone prize bars of chocolate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wild' rearranges REVELS. 'Prize' is spoken for 'prise' (to force open), so 'prise bars' are crowbars.
explanation.definitionFit: Crowbars used to force things open are the classic tools for prising.

clue.text: A foreigner we can't fault, though we have no idea who he is

definitions.text: we have no idea who he is

parts.note: something we cannot fault is flawless, i.e. perfect
a stranger is an outsider or foreigner

explanation.surface: A flawless foreigner whose identity is a complete mystery.
explanation.definitionFit: A person entirely unknown to us is a complete unknown, someone we have never met.

clue.text: Its contents are still to be dealt with

definitions.text: Its contents are still to be dealt with

parts.words: Its contents are still to be dealt with
parts.note: describes the office tray holding paperwork that has arrived and awaits attention

explanation.walkthrough: 'Dealt with' might suggest cards; it is office paperwork awaiting action.
explanation.definitionFit: The desk tray for incoming papers holds work awaiting action.

clue.text: Freshly made drink flavoured with honey

indicators.note: freshly suggests making anew, so the letters of the word made are put together afresh in a new order

explanation.walkthrough: 'Freshly' rearranges MADE.
explanation.definitionFit: This ancient fermented beverage is brewed from honey and water.

clue.text: Revised tax code that is right savagely censured?

indicators.note: a revised version is reworked, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: i.e. is the abbreviation of id est, 'that is'

explanation.surface: A taxpayer is harshly criticised for an amended tax code.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Revised' rearranges TAX, CODE, IE and R together.
explanation.definitionFit: To flay someone verbally is to criticise them fiercely; literally the word means stripping off skin.

clue.text: Plate was her great help in the kitchen

parts.note: a plate is a dish
taken as written

explanation.surface: A plate was a handy aid to a woman cooking.
explanation.definitionFit: A machine that cleans crockery saves a great deal of work at the sink.

clue.text: Make a solemn declaration to cut a new seat out

indicators.note: out here means outside, so the rearranged seat wraps around the word for cut
a new seat is a remade one, so the letters of seat are rearranged

parts.note: to cut is to sever

explanation.surface: Someone vows to slash a replacement seat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'New' rearranges SEAT into SATE; 'out' puts SATE outside SEVER, giving SSEVERATE, after A.
explanation.definitionFit: To affirm something earnestly and formally is to state it as a solemn truth.

clue.text: Isn't content with talking when going round Connecticut?

indicators.note: going round says the word for when encircles the state abbreviation

parts.note: as can mean when ('as he left')
CT is the postal abbreviation for the US state of Connecticut

explanation.surface: Someone touring Connecticut wants more than mere talk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Going round' puts AS around CT. Someone not content with talk takes action.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who prefers deeds to words does things rather than talks.

clue.text: Employed as a device for keeping things in suspense, maybe

definitions.text: Employed as a device for keeping things in suspense, maybe

parts.words: Employed as a device for keeping things in suspense, maybe
parts.note: 'keeping things in suspense' reads as creating tension, but literally means keeping things hanging up, as a hook on a wall does

explanation.walkthrough: 'In suspense' suggests a thriller's tension; it means hanging, like a coat on a hook.
explanation.definitionFit: A wall hook keeps coats suspended, so something put to work as one serves that purpose.

clue.text: Nearly unable to see things clearly

definitions.text: Nearly unable to see things clearly

parts.words: Nearly unable to see things clearly
parts.note: 'Nearly' reads as 'almost' but is meant as 'at close range': such a person cannot see near things clearly

explanation.walkthrough: 'Nearly' looks like 'almost' but means 'up close': a long-sighted person cannot focus on nearby things. The word also means prudent.
explanation.definitionFit: Long-sighted people see distant objects well but blur close ones.

clue.text: Prestigious London club magazine

definitions.meaning: a famous north London football club, nicknamed the Gunners
a magazine is a store of weapons and ammunition

explanation.definitionFit: The football club is named after the Woolwich armaments works; a store of weapons is the military sense of magazine.

clue.text: Scared of seeing a beginner with a gun?

parts.note: L is a learner, from the L-plate a learner driver displays
someone carrying a gun is armed

explanation.surface: Frightened at the sight of a novice wielding a gun.
explanation.walkthrough: L for learner comes from British L-plates on learner drivers' cars.
explanation.definitionFit: Frightened and fearful are the same state as being made anxious by danger.

clue.text: Greatly transformed sort of gallery

indicators.note: a transformed sort of something is a changed form of it, so the letters of gallery are rearranged

explanation.surface: An art gallery has been greatly made over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Transformed sort of' rearranges GALLERY.
explanation.definitionFit: Both mean to a great extent, for the most part.

clue.text: Plays for time outside All Saints?

indicators.note: outside says the abbreviation for saints sits on either side of the word all

parts.note: STS is the abbreviation for saints (plural of St)
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone delays matters outside a church named All Saints.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Outside' puts STS around ALL.
explanation.definitionFit: To delay deliberately, hoping to gain time, is to temporise.

clue.text: Retrospective anxiety about a strong-scented herb

indicators.note: about says the reversed word goes round the letter a
retrospective means looking back, so the word for anxiety is read backwards

parts.note: anxiety is worry

explanation.surface: Worry looking back over a pungent garden plant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Retrospective' turns WORRY into YRROW; 'about' puts that around A.
explanation.definitionFit: Achillea, a feathery-leaved plant with a pungent smell, is a common wild herb.

clue.text: Calls for help when in dire peril

definitions.text: Calls for help when in dire peril

parts.words: Calls for help when in dire peril
parts.note: describes the alerts, such as flares or SOS, sent out by ships or people in danger

explanation.definitionFit: Mayday calls and flares are emergency alerts sent when lives are at risk.

clue.text: Accepted responsibility for a change of design

indicators.note: a change of design is a new arrangement, so the letters of design are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone took charge of a redesign.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Change of' rearranges DESIGN.
explanation.definitionFit: Putting your name to a document commits you to it, so you have accepted it formally.

clue.text: A lot of things held up in the same generator?

indicators.note: in says the reversed word goes inside the word for the same

parts.note: do is short for ditto, meaning the same

indicators.note: in a down clue, held up means the word is written upwards, i.e. backwards

parts.note: a lot of things are many

explanation.surface: Is the generator holding up lots of the same items?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Held up' reverses MANY to YNAM, which goes 'in' DO (ditto).
explanation.definitionFit: A machine that turns motion into electric current produces power.

clue.text: A wind sock at an airport that holds the record?

definitions.text: A wind sock at an airport
definitions.meaning: a windsock is a fabric tube showing wind direction
the card or paper cover that a vinyl record is kept in

explanation.definitionFit: Both a windsock's fabric tube and a record's cover are tube- or pocket-shaped coverings.

clue.text: Can be made to assist a blockage in the circulation

indicators.note: can be made to says the letters of assist may be reformed into another word

explanation.surface: Helping can be turned into an obstruction to blood flow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Can be made to' rearranges ASSIST.
explanation.definitionFit: In medicine the word means a stoppage of the flow of blood or other body fluid.

clue.text: One of America's best-known soaps

parts.note: soaps could be bars of soap, but here a television soap opera of the 1980s about the rich Carrington family

explanation.walkthrough: 'Soaps' looks like toiletries; it is soap operas.
explanation.definitionFit: This 1980s American prime-time drama about an oil family was a hugely popular soap opera.

clue.text: But it isn't the most important part of an orange

definitions.text: But it isn't the most important part of an orange

parts.words: But it isn't the most important part of an orange
parts.note: the word means the essence or core of a matter, yet in an orange it is the bitter white layer under the peel

explanation.walkthrough: The word means the central essence of anything, but on an orange it is the white layer under the peel, hardly the important bit.
explanation.definitionFit: Figuratively the core of a matter; literally the white spongy layer beneath citrus rind.

clue.text: Futile report on a listless student, perhaps

definitions.meaning: futile means hopeless or not feasible

definitions.text: report on a listless student, perhaps
definitions.meaning: a school report on a pupil lacking energy might say the student has ..., i.e. no drive

explanation.definitionFit: A hopeless project is a non-starter; a pupil with no drive lacks get-up-and-go.

clue.text: We turn up a footnote about service accommodation

indicators.note: about says the footnote abbreviation wraps around the reversed word

parts.note: PS, postscript, is a note added at the foot of a letter

indicators.note: in a down clue, turn up means the word is written upwards, i.e. backwards

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: We spot a footnote that deals with lodgings for servicemen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turn up' reverses WE to EW; 'about' puts PS around it. 'Service' is a church service, not the armed forces.
explanation.definitionFit: Church benches seat the congregation during worship.

clue.text: sizable gem — the biggest in the collection?

definitions.meaning: split differently, the letters say 'the biggest one' of a set

explanation.definitionFit: A big jewel is a sizable gem; with the break moved four letters on, the same letters say the biggest one.

clue.text: French author's plebian guide!

definitions.note: author's is read as 'author is', so the definition is the author himself

indicators.note: plebeian means not upper-class, i.e. non-U, so the letter U for upper class is dropped

explanation.surface: A French writer's guidebook for the common people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plebian' (non-U, common) removes U, the letter for upper class in the U and non-U usage of 1950s Britain, from GUIDE. André Gide was a Nobel-winning French novelist.
explanation.definitionFit: André Gide was a French novelist and Nobel laureate.

clue.text: Suitable footwear for ladies, in-waiting?

parts.note: ladies-in-waiting attend at a royal court, so their footwear would be shoes for court; also plain women's low-cut pumps

explanation.walkthrough: The comma splits 'ladies-in-waiting', royal attendants at court; the British name for women's plain low-cut pumps fits shoes worn at court.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain low-heeled women's pumps carry the British name of the royal household.
